original_title: (Arylsulfonyl)acetonitrile as an Efficient Unified Reagent for the Photocatalyzed Hydrosulfonylation of Alkenes
title: One reagent, two jobs, in alkene hydrosulfonylation
blurb: Arylsulfonylacetonitriles both throw the sulfonyl radical, via photocatalytic C-S cleavage, and hand over the hydrogen atom that finishes the job, so one reagent replaces what usually takes two. Broad scope and good functional group tolerance across a fairly diverse set of sulfones.

original_title: Palladium-Catalyzed Three-Component Synthesis of Dihydrobenzofurans from Aryl Iodides, Norbornene, and H2O2
title: H2O2 as the oxygen source in a Pd/norbornene annulation
blurb: Aryl iodides plus a norbornene plus H2O2 build dihydrobenzofurans, with the peroxide acting as both oxidant and the source of the oxygen atoms that end up in the ring. H2O2 also happily oxidizes Pd(0) and norbornene and falls apart to O2 on its own, so the whole cycle only survives because they drip the peroxide in slowly and pick the right base.

original_title: Antibody-drug conjugate shows promising early results in Phase I trial in sarcoma patients - Medical Xpress
title: An ADC posts early sarcoma numbers
blurb: Phase I data on an antibody-drug conjugate in sarcoma patients, called promising. That's a small, early readout, so file it under maybe for now rather than a win.

original_title: Histatin-1-loaded nanovesicular hydrogel for sustained peptide delivery, biofilm disruption, and healing of infected diabetic wounds
title: A hydrogel that drips Histatin-1 onto infected diabetic wounds
blurb: Nanovesicles loaded with the antimicrobial peptide Histatin-1 sit inside an in-situ gel that releases the peptide slowly, breaks up biofilm, calms inflammation, and pushes angiogenesis along to close infected diabetic wounds faster.

original_title: Isolable crystalline oxoboranes
title: Oxoboranes finally isolated, six decades after people started trying
blurb: A B-O triple bond on a two-coordinate boron has been theorized and chased since the 1960s but always vanished before anyone could get it in a bottle. Two separate groups now report crystalline oxoboranes, neutral and cationic versions, built off related diboracumulenes, stable enough to actually sit there and be looked at.

original_title: Catalytic Activation of “Orbital-Symmetry-Forbidden” Pericyclic Reactions
title: How catalysts talk their way around orbital-symmetry bans
blurb: Some pericyclic reactions are forbidden by orbital symmetry no matter how favorable the thermodynamics, and that's been especially stubborn for converting high-energy photoisomers back down. This is a systematic look at how chemically different catalysts actually get around that constraint, mechanistically, rather than just reporting that they do.

original_title: Dual-responsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-methacrylic acid) hydrogels: role and synergies of pH and temperature in tailoring hydrogel responsiveness.
title: Tuning a hydrogel with heat and pH together
blurb: A PNIPAM/methacrylic acid hydrogel where temperature and pH response aren't separate knobs but work in tandem to set how the gel swells and releases. Title's doing most of the talking here, there isn't much else to go on.

original_title: Photoredox‐Catalyzed Dearomative Spirocyclization of Biaryl Ynones With Fluoroalkyl Carboxylic Anhydrides to Access Fluoroalkylated Spiro[5.5]trienones
title: Fluoroalkyl radicals build spiro trienones from biaryl ynones
blurb: Photoredox dearomative spirocyclization using cheap fluoroalkyl carboxylic anhydrides as the CF2H/CF2Cl radical source and acetoxime as activator, redox-neutral, no extra oxidant needed. Over 50 spiro[5.5]trienones made this way, it scales to grams, and they show the scaffold can be derivatized further.

original_title: Optimizing radiobiological effects of(119)Sb targeted radionuclide therapy via DNA incorporation: a Monte Carlo simulation study.
title: Sb-119 Auger therapy, modeled before anyone injects it
blurb: A Monte Carlo study tunes the radiobiology of Sb-119 targeted therapy by incorporating it directly into DNA, chasing the short-range Auger damage that only matters if you get that close to the genome. Simulation only, so it's a design exercise ahead of any actual dosing.

original_title: eRoboChem: Autonomous Electrosynthesis Across Redox Modes and Reactor Designs
title: A self-driving lab for electrosynthesis
blurb: eRoboChem automates the fiddly parts of electrochemistry, electrode choice, reactor design, electron transfer, by running automated experiments with analytical feedback and Bayesian optimization across different redox modes and reactor setups. Electrosynthesis has real upside but the optimization overhead is exactly what scares synthetic chemists off, which is the problem this is aimed at.

original_title: Radical detour in photocatalyst–enzyme pairs
title: 180 photoredox-enzyme pairings turn up one good radical coupling
blurb: Pairing photoredox catalysts with enzymes opens reactivity neither gets to alone, and a systematic screen of 180 combinations found a C(sp3)-C(sp3) radical cross-coupling you can steer to either the β- or γ-carbon. That steerability is the actual news, it's what turns an otherwise generic radical coupling into a route to non-canonical amino acids.

original_title: AtomVie, ITM Sign Lutetium-177 Supply Deal for Radiopharma Manufacturing - Contract Pharma
title: ITM locks down more lutetium-177 before the radiopharma queue gets longer
blurb: AtomVie signs on to supply Lu-177 for ITM's manufacturing. Not science, just plumbing, but isotope supply is the thing actually gating how many of these radioligand therapies get made.

original_title: Photoredox‑Catalyzed Regioselective C−H Functionalization of Aliphatic Amines: Access to α‑Tertiary Amine‑Substituted Difluorocyclopropenes
title: Difluorocyclopropenes finally get an amine handle
blurb: Nobody had managed to put an aliphatic amine on a difluorocyclopropene before. A photoredox late-stage functionalization does it under mild conditions, regioselectively, and on substrates complex enough to matter, landing α-tertiary amine motifs on a ring class that's usually just a synthetic intermediate.

original_title: Catalyst-Free Solid-State Dearomative Cycloaddition Driven by Pressure-Induced Proton-Gating
title: Crushing aromatics into 3D shapes, no catalyst, no light
blurb: Dearomative cycloadditions normally need photocatalysts or rough conditions to turn flat aromatic rings into the 3D scaffolds drugs actually want. This one runs in the solid state at room temperature, self-catalyzed by pressure-induced proton gating in the gigapascal range, through an inverse-electron-demand mechanism. Trading photocatalysts for gigapascal pressure isn't a free lunch, but it's catalyst-free and light-free, which is the whole pitch.
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters

original_title: A Solvent‐Controlled Chemodivergent Cycloaddition of Quinone Esters With Enaminones
title: Same two reagents, different solvent, different ring system
blurb: Quinone esters plus enaminones can go two ways: a C2,C1-selective (2+3) cycloaddition or a C2,C3'-selective (3+3), and which one you get is picked just by swapping solvent. One path gives tetrahydrocarbazoles, the other isoquinolinones, with downstream chemistry included to show the products aren't dead ends.

original_title: An International Study of Factors Affecting Variability of Dosimetry Calculations, Part 6: Lessons Learned, Achievable Variability, and the Road Ahead
title: Six papers in, dosimetry calculations still don't agree with each other
blurb: Part 6 of an international series on why dose calculations vary between centers, closing out with what variability is actually achievable and what's still left to fix. Not a result so much as a reckoning after five prior installments.

original_title: Rhodium-Catalyzed Asymmetric Transformation of 2-(Aryldimethylsilyl)benzyl α,β-Unsaturated Carboxylates into β-Substituted Indanones: A Method of Enabling a Rhodium 1,4-Shift
title: Getting rhodium to do the 1,4-shift it didn't want to do
blurb: The aryl-Rh 1,4-addition/1,4-shift route to indanones works fine for β,β-disubstituted substrates, but the β-monosubstituted case stalls because the shift to the aryl ortho position is sluggish. Swapping in a 2-(aryldimethylsilyl)benzyl group suppresses the side reactions enough to make the shift happen, giving enantioenriched β-substituted indanones that were previously out of reach.

original_title: Enantioselective Tsuji–Trost Reaction of Acyclic Fluoroenolates Using P-Chiral PHOX
title: A P-chiral PHOX ligand beats the standard one on fluorinated stereocenters
blurb: Tsuji-Trost on acyclic fluoroenolates to make chiral tertiary alkyl fluorides, and the usual commercial (S)-t-Bu-PHOX loses out to a P-chiral version. Putting the bulky arene anti to the t-Bu group on the oxazoline, instead of the epimeric arrangement, is what pushes the enantioselectivity up.

original_title: Ir(III)-Catalyzed Direct Arylation of Oxindoles with Diazoquinones for Regioselective Access to Alkylated Benzocarbazoles and a TMC-95A Intermediate
title: One Ir(III) catalyst, two different arylation outcomes depending on solvent
blurb: Arylating oxindoles with diazoquinones under Ir(III) catalysis gives either 2,6-alkylarylated anilines or C7-arylated oxindoles, just by switching solvent, through a quinoid-carbene intermediate that cleaves an amide bond before directing the C-H arylation. The payoff is a library of alkylated benzocarbazoles and an intermediate toward TMC-95A, so it's not just a methodology flex.

original_title: Defluoro–Dechloro Dearomative [5,5]‐Rearrangement–Diels–Alder Cascade Toward Naphthalene Construction
title: Naphthalenes built by shedding fluorine and chlorine along the way
blurb: Fluorinated aryl sulfoxides and β,γ-unsaturated nitriles run a [5,5]-sigmatropic rearrangement into unstable dearomatized sulfonium salts, which then do a Diels-Alder with chlorinated dienes. The cascade finishes by kicking out both the fluorine and chlorine to rearomatize into multisubstituted naphthalenes, using the halogens as leaving groups instead of just passengers.

original_title: A generative neural network architecture for structure elucidation
title: A structure-elucidation model trained on real NMR spectra, not simulated ones
blurb: Deep learning models that guess molecular structure from 1H/13C NMR usually train on simulated spectra and faceplant on real experimental data. This transformer skips that gap by training purely on experimental spectra instead. Training on reality instead of simulation is the obvious fix, and apparently nobody had done it properly until now.

original_title: RamanGPT maps bidirectionally between crystal structures and Raman spectra of inorganic materials
title: RamanGPT goes both ways between crystal structure and Raman spectrum
blurb: Normally you either simulate a Raman spectrum from structure via DFT, which is slow, or guess structure from spectrum by matching against a curated reference library, which only works for what's already catalogued. RamanGPT trains an ALIGNN model on a 5,099-material database to handle the forward direction and runs it in reverse for the inverse problem. Whether the inverse step holds up on materials outside that training set is the part worth watching.

original_title: PharmaLogic buys Lantheus' New Jersey radiopharma plant with a supply deal attached - MarketScale
title: PharmaLogic buys Lantheus' New Jersey radiopharma plant, supply deal attached
blurb: PharmaLogic picks up Lantheus' New Jersey radiopharmaceutical manufacturing plant along with an attached supply agreement. Consolidation in radiopharma manufacturing, not a science story.

original_title: Transatlantic Oncology Experts Review Targeted Radiopharmaceutical Therapies and Clinical Delivery Challenges - Bioengineer.org
title: A transatlantic panel on why targeted radiopharmaceuticals are hard to actually deliver
blurb: Oncology experts from both sides of the Atlantic comparing notes on targeted radiopharmaceutical therapies, with the focus on clinical delivery logistics rather than new chemistry.

original_title: Calcium catalysed nucleophilic fluorination
title: Calcium steps in for the usual fluorination catalysts
blurb: A calcium-catalyzed route to nucleophilic fluorination, swapping in a cheap, abundant metal for chemistry that normally leans on fussier catalysts.

original_title: Lysine-R2HGylation-C5 identified as a post-translational modification in R2HG-elevated cancers
title: R2HG has a second trick besides blocking enzymes
blurb: The oncometabolite R2HG is known for noncovalently inhibiting αKG-dependent enzymes in IDH-mutant cancers. This paper finds it also covalently glues onto lysines, a modification the authors name lysine-R2HGylation, and they built R2HG-mimicking probes to actually map which lysines and where. A second, covalent mechanism for a metabolite that already had plenty to answer for.

original_title: Aquaporin biomonomer functionalized GUVs crosslinked cryogenic membrane for selective ammonia separation.
title: Aquaporin-studded vesicles as an ammonia-sieving membrane
blurb: Giant unilamellar vesicles functionalized with aquaporin biomonomers, crosslinked into a cryogenic membrane built for selective ammonia separation. Bio-inspired membrane engineering aimed at gas separation rather than the usual drug delivery angle for GUVs.

original_title: Automated In-House Radiosynthesis Yields High-Purity Prostate Cancer - Bioengineer.org
title: An automated, in-house radiosynthesis setup for high-purity prostate cancer material
blurb: An automated radiosynthesis workflow built to produce high-purity prostate cancer radiopharmaceutical in-house. The win here is throughput and quality control, not new chemistry.

original_title: Electrocatalytic C–H Trifluoromethylation of Benzo-Fused Indolizines Using TT–CF3+OTf–
title: Trifluoromethylating indolizines with electricity instead of a metal catalyst
blurb: Regioselective C(sp2)-H trifluoromethylation of benzo-fused indolizines using Ritter's reagent as the CF3 source, run electrochemically with no metal catalyst and no external oxidant. Good yields on both electron-rich and electron-poor substrates, the authors argue for a radical pathway, and they claim it scales.

original_title: Globally antiaromatic anthracene–porphyrin nanobelts
title: Porphyrin nanobelts that are antiaromatic the whole way around
blurb: Anthracene-bridged porphyrin nanobelts built via nickel(0) coupling and Scholl oxidation, with Hückel circuits of 72, 96, or 120 π electrons. Conjugated belts get chased for their radial orbitals and odd electronic behavior, but landing global antiaromaticity at that electron count is the actual news here.

original_title: Biocatalytic Total Synthesis of (−)-Ambuic Acid
title: The mirror-image ambuic acid, made in 14 steps
blurb: First total synthesis of the (−)-enantiomer, the one nature didn't bother making. They borrowed the known route to the natural antipode but trimmed it to 14 steps from commercial material, with a late-stage biocatalytic reduction converting an epoxydiketone cleanly to a single stereo- and regioisomer of the alcohol, the kind of step that usually needs babysitting with a chemocatalyst.

original_title: Advanced Analytical Techniques for Identification and Quantification of Impurities in Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients - Review Article
title: No single method catches every API impurity
blurb: A review of the analytical toolbox for tracking down impurities in drug substances, covering everything from starting materials and intermediates to degradation products. The point is practical: impurities differ enough in polarity, mass, and structure that no one technique covers them all, so you're stuck running several in parallel.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Extraframework Cations Promoted Ultratrace Acetylene Capture by Coordinatively Unsaturated Nickel Sites in FAU Zeolites
title: Trapping acetylene at the parts-per-million level
blurb: A dual-cation trick in FAU zeolites, nickel paired with barium, pulls acetylene out of ethylene streams down to ppm concentrations with selectivity over 100, which matters because ultratrace alkyne removal for polymer- and electronic-grade olefins is normally a slog. Neutron diffraction and DFT pin the effect on exactly where the Ba2+ sits in the framework, not just on the coordinatively unsaturated Ni sites.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Universal Transfer Reagents for the Synthesis of Carbon‐Labeled Methyl, Fluoromethyl, and Difluoromethyl Motifs
title: One reagent family for 13C- and 14C-tagged CF2H groups
blurb: Carbon-labeled sulfoximines built from primary isotopic sources that act as C1-transfer agents, handing you labeled difluoromethyl compounds plus monofluoromethyl, cyclopropane, and epoxide analogs from the same stock. Isotopically labeling the CF2H group has been a real pain point in med chem, so a general, practical route to it is worth something on its own.

original_title: Alcohol-Enabled Telescoped Synthesis of Phenolic Phosphine Oxides and Fluorinated Variants for Redox-Neutral Mitsunobu Reactions
title: Turning alcohols straight into phosphine oxide catalysts, no stops along the way
blurb: An alcohol-enabled Michaelis-Arbuzov rearrangement telescopes phosphinite formation and a substoichiometric alkyl-bromide-promoted rearrangement into one solvent-free sequence, skipping the usual intermediate isolation. It lands you diarylphosphine oxides, fluorinated ones included, for redox-neutral Mitsunobu chemistry, shorter than the substrate-specific routes people normally reach for.

original_title: Unlocking exceptional electrocatalysis via short-range phase segregation in helical Boerdijk–Coxeter nanowires
title: Phase-segregated helical nanowires for electrocatalysis
blurb: Dendritic nanowires with a Boerdijk-Coxeter helical structure that segregate into phases rather than staying single-phase, and the combination of moderate lattice strain with a (111)-preferred structure is what's credited for better adsorption kinetics and longer-term stability. No word on which reaction or how it stacks up against the usual catalysts, so that comparison is still owed.

original_title: Designer proteins for asymmetric photocatalysis
title: Designer proteins doing photocatalysis's stereochemistry work
blurb: Engineered protein scaffolds pressed into service for asymmetric photocatalysis, using protein design to steer which enantiomer comes out of a light-driven reaction.

original_title: Quantifying effective radiation doses from <sup>13</sup>N-ammonia PET/CT procedures for myocardial perfusion imaging
title: Clocking the radiation dose from a N-13 ammonia heart scan
blurb: A dosimetry study totting up effective radiation doses from N-13-ammonia PET/CT myocardial perfusion scans, the bookkeeping work behind deciding how often someone can reasonably get one.

original_title: Palladium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Oxidative Remote (4 + 1)-Cyclization of 1,6-Enynes
title: A chiral route to cyclopentane-fused lactones from enynes
blurb: Palladium catalysis turns 1,6-enynes into cyclopentane-fused lactones and lactams via a remote (4+1) cyclization, using PhI(OPiv)2 as the oxidant and chiral pyridinyl-oxazoline ligands for the enantioselectivity. Both the Z- and E-enyne isomers work, and TFE as solvent is critical for actually getting the chemoselectivity and ee, not just a nice-to-have.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Synthesis and preclinical evaluation of [99mTc]Tc-quercetin for preferential accumulation at experimental Escherichia coli infection sites: a preclinical feasibility study
title: A radiolabeled quercetin tracer for finding E. coli infections
blurb: Tc-99m-tagged quercetin tested in a preclinical feasibility study for imaging E. coli infection sites, banking on the flavonoid preferentially piling up where the infection is. Early days and animal-only data, but a cheap natural-product tracer beating the usual radiolabeled antibiotics would be a nice trick if it holds up.

original_title: An International Study of Factors Affecting Variability of Dosimetry Calculations, Part 6: Lessons Learned, Achievable Variability, and the Road Ahead.
title: Dosimetry variability study wraps up with a six-part verdict
blurb: The final installment of an international multi-lab effort to pin down why dose calculations disagree, landing on what variability is actually achievable and where to go from here. Took six parts to get there.

original_title: Synergistic Pd/Ag C8-Functionalization of Xanthines: Merging C–H Activation of Xanthines with Z-Selective Hydropivalation of Alkynes
title: Caffeine gets a Pd/Ag tag-team makeover at C8
blurb: A palladium/silver duo does C-H alkynylation and Z-selective hydropivalation of arylacetylenes in one pot, loading caffeine and other xanthines up at C8 in 70-80% yield across a broad scope. DFT backs a genuinely cooperative Pd/Ag mechanism, not just two catalysts taking turns.

original_title: A Convenient One-Pot Route to [Thianthrenium][B(C 6 F 5 ) 4 ]
title: A one-pot shortcut to a strong radical-cation oxidant
blurb: [Thianthrenium][B(C6F5)4] is a handy outer-sphere one-electron oxidant, but making it usually means nitrosonium oxidation or salt metathesis in liquid SO2, or MeCN that can linger and mess with whatever reaction comes next. This route gets there in one pot, which mostly matters if you've ever had to source SO2 glassware.

original_title: Dual photoresponsive hydrogel surfaces enabling integrated single-cell analysis of morphology and gene expression
title: A hydrogel that photographs cells, then lets go of the interesting ones
blurb: One photoresponsive layer traps cells with light, the other degrades on command to release them once you've imaged them, so you can track morphology over time and then pull specific cells out for gene expression analysis. Dense, evenly spaced arrays mean actual throughput instead of hunting single cells under a scope.

original_title: FAIR NMR: Acquisition, Processing, and Modeling of Time-Resolved NMR Data According to the FAIR Principles
title: Giving kinetic NMR data the FAIR treatment it's never had
blurb: A workflow for acquiring, processing, and kinetic-modeling time-resolved NMR data that's built to be reused across labs, instead of locked in whatever ad hoc pipeline and incomplete metadata each group happens to use. Useful mainly if people actually adopt the metadata conventions, which is always the catch with FAIR anything.

original_title: Rational Optimization of a Peptide-Guided Delivery System Enhances Macrophage Targeting and Drug Biodistribution toward Inflammation
title: Tuning up a macrophage-homing peptide so the drug actually goes where the inflammation is
blurb: Builds on their earlier CRV peptide, which binds RXR-beta to home in on macrophages, with a rational optimization pass that improves both macrophage targeting and overall biodistribution toward inflamed tissue. The point is hitting macrophages at the inflammation site instead of macrophages everywhere.

original_title: Organophotocatalytic hydrosilylation of unactivated α,β-unsaturated amides via aminyl radical-activated silylboronates
title: Light-driven hydrosilylation that doesn't need an activated alkene
blurb: Visible-light photoredox generates an aminyl radical that wakes up a silylboronate, letting it hydrosilylate plain, unactivated alpha,beta-unsaturated amides under mild conditions. Broad scope, runs at gram scale, and works on late-stage drug molecules, which is the part that'll actually get it used.

original_title: Synthesis of Chiral β-Amino Amides via Bioinspired Ring-Opening Aminolysis of β-Lactams
title: Stealing a trick from beta-lactamases to make chiral amino amides
blurb: A dinuclear zinc catalyst mimics how metallo-beta-lactamases chew through beta-lactams, using that biomimetic ring-opening to kinetically resolve racemic beta-lactams with aliphatic amines. Out the other end: enantioenriched beta-amino amides and leftover beta-lactams, both with high ee.

original_title: Enhancing Grignard Reactions via Anion Borrowing in Deep Eutectic/Organic Biphasic Media
title: Why dumping your Grignard into a deep eutectic solvent actually helps
blurb: Deep eutectic solvents are already known to boost Grignard additions, so this one digs into why, running ab initio MD, QM/MM, and enhanced sampling on iPrMgCl plus acetophenone. The DES looks to be borrowing the anion away from the Grignard, which is a mechanistic answer rather than a new reaction.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis
title: A DNA typewriter wrote down an entire mouse's cell lineage, zygote to organs
blurb: Uses the DNA Typewriter recording system to trace cell lineage continuously from the fertilized egg through late organogenesis, in an actual mouse. A lineage tree built from the embryo's own DNA as it developed, not pieced together after the fact.

original_title: Composition-Driven Discovery of Multimetallic Catalysts Using Features Inspired by the Virtual Crystal Approximation
title: Letting composition stand in for structure in catalyst screening
blurb: ML descriptors built from a virtual-crystal-approximation-style composition average, skipping the structural enumeration multimetallic catalysts normally demand. The pitch is you don't need to know where every atom sits on a surface that reconstructs under operating conditions anyway, just what's in the mix.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Supramolecular Regulation of the Enzymatic Dephosphorylation of Twin Phosphotyrosine Peptides
title: A molecular cage that reaches in and tunes a phosphatase's grip
blurb: A synthetic pseudopeptidic cage with an aromatic pocket sized for twin phosphotyrosine motifs and ammonium arms that grab the phosphates, shown to actually modulate enzymatic dephosphorylation of those peptides in water. Binding data backs it up, but it's a designed receptor doing the regulating, not biology.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Synthesis of Lignans from the Biobased Platform Chemical Itaconic Acid Using Pd-Catalyzed Coupling Reactions
title: Lignans out of itaconic acid instead of petrochemicals
blurb: Pd-catalyzed coupling of itaconic acid diesters and monoesters with arene diazonium salts, run at room temperature with no ligand or base, feeds into gossypidien and jatrodien plus related dibenzylbutenolide and arylidene-butyrolactone lignans two or three steps later. A biobased starting material standing in for the usual ones, worth it if those extra steps don't eat the savings.

original_title: Benchmarking and Discovery of Ligands for Sterically Challenging Copper-Catalyzed C–N Cross-Couplings
title: Stress-testing Cu amination ligands where the sterics actually bite
blurb: Seven ligands run across 30 aryl halides, iodides, bromides, and chlorides with varying ortho bulk, and two amines, nearly 500 reactions, to see which Cu-catalyzed C-N couplings survive real steric demand instead of the easy substrates everyone reports. Reads more like a reference table than a discovery paper, which is exactly the point.

original_title: Bioisosteric sulfoxonium ylides as building blocks for accessing thiazole derivatives using flow chemistry
title: Thiazoles on tap, made from bioisosteric ylides in flow
blurb: A packed-bed flow setup generates alpha-keto sulfoxonium ylides on the fly and runs them straight into 2-aminothiazole synthesis, tolerating a wide range of thioureas and thioamides. The actual selling point is that swapping in these bioisosteres reportedly boosts aqueous solubility and cuts lipophilicity versus the strained scaffolds they're replacing, not the flow rig itself.

original_title: Atomic structure engineering of iridium on niobium pentoxide for selectivity-switchable CER, EOP, and 3e − ORR electrocatalysis
title: Dialing iridium from single atoms to nanoparticles to pick your electrochemistry
blurb: Same Ir/Nb2O5 system, different Ir dispersion, and the product shifts: chlorine evolution, electrochemical oxidation, or the 3-electron oxygen reduction to peroxide. A tunable-dispersion knob standing in for three separate optimized catalysts.

original_title: Decoding C–O versus C–C Bond Selectivity in Nickel–Metallaphotoredox Carboxylic Acid Cross-Couplings
title: Why nickel-photoredox sometimes picks C-O over C-C
blurb: Same carboxylic acid/aryl halide coupling under nickel-photoredox dual catalysis, but the aryl halide's identity turns out to be the switch deciding whether you get a C-C or a C-O bond. DFT plus electrochemistry finally explains a selectivity split that's been hiding behind 'deceptively similar conditions.'

original_title: Phosphine Catalyzed Enantioselective and Diastereospecific [3 + 2] Cyclization to Construct Spirocyclic Azetidines
title: One phosphine, two routes to spirocyclic azetidines
blurb: A tartaric-acid-derived DIOP phosphine catalyzes [3+2] cyclizations between azetidine enones and either allenoates or butynoates, landing spiro-cyclopentene azetidines at 87-98% ee and over 20:1 dr. They ran it gram-scale too, so it's not just a fume-hood curiosity.

original_title: Photoredox Chloroarylation of Electron-Deficient Alkenes: One-Pot Formation of β-Lactams
title: A chlorine radical tame enough to build beta-lactam precursors
blurb: Visible-light photoredox generates a chlorine radical that pyridine complexation keeps stable enough for selective Truce-Smiles chloroarylation of electron-deficient alkenes, giving alpha-aryl-beta-chloro amides with broad functional group tolerance. The same one-pot setup extends to aminoarylation of acrylamides, so the tamed radical turns out to be the reusable part.

original_title: Enantiospecific Synthesis of 1‐Pyrrolines by Gold Catalysis
title: Turning L-serine into enantiopure 1-pyrrolines with gold
blurb: Commercial N-Boc-L-serine becomes enantiopure propargylglycine methyl ester in four steps and 35% overall, then AuCl3-catalyzed intramolecular cycloisomerization closes it into 2,5-disubstituted 1-pyrrolines enantiospecifically. A cheap chiral-pool amino acid doing the job that usually needs an asymmetric catalysis step of its own.

original_title: Machine Learning-Assisted Image Analysis of Sub-visible Particles in Biologics Drug Products: A Comparative Study Using Micro-Flow Imaging and FlowCam
title: Teaching software to tell contaminant particles apart
blurb: A deep-learning pipeline bolts transfer-learning feature extraction onto anomaly detection and similarity search, aimed at the real problem with MFI and FlowCam images: you can count and shape-sort particles all day, but figuring out what a particle actually is and where it came from is the hard part. Payoff is better ground truth labeling, not just a prettier scatter plot.

original_title: Low-Energy Photon-Mediated Skeletal Editing of Indole to Quinazoline via a Nitrogen Insertion Reaction
title: Swapping a carbon for a nitrogen in indole, no oxidant required
blurb: Low-energy photoredox pries open indole's ring via a singlet-oxygen intermediate, then lets ammonia stitch a nitrogen back in to deliver a quinazoline, skipping the stoichiometric oxidants skeletal editing usually needs. Broad substrate tolerance claimed, which is the part worth checking.

original_title: Three‐Component Regiodivergent Carboamination of Fluorinated Dienes
title: One diene, two different products, just switch the ligand
blurb: Fluorinated 1,3-dienes stand in for gem-difluorocyclopropanes as a route to 1,3-disubstituted 2-fluoroallylic scaffolds, and palladium carboamination picks 1,2- or 1,4-addition purely on which ligand you load. Regiodivergence on demand from one catalytic system is the actual selling point.

original_title: Pro/Ala/Ser (PAS) peptides as an alternative to polyethylene glycol (PEG) for the surface shielding of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) carrying therapeutic mRNA
title: Swapping PEG on mRNA-LNPs for a peptide shield instead
blurb: PASylation, a Pro/Ala/Ser peptide coating, swaps in for PEGylated lipids on mRNA-LNP surfaces, aimed squarely at the anti-PEG antibodies that are getting more common in the general population. Fixes an immunogenicity problem only if the peptide shields the particle in circulation as well as PEG does.

original_title: Molecular Miniaturization of Carbon–Nitrogen‐Coupled Biphenylmethyl Radicals Enables Efficient Near‐Infrared Electroluminescence
title: Shrinking a radical emitter so it can actually be evaporated into a device
blurb: Carbon-nitrogen-coupled BTM radicals make good NIR emitters once donor engineering boosts their quantum yield, but the bulky donors that help also push molecular weight and sublimation temperature past the point where vacuum thermal evaporation still works. This miniaturization strategy trims the molecule back down so it can still go into a device the normal way.

original_title: Regiospecific Sila‐Matteson Homologative Arylation of Biased ( N ‐Oxide) Azines
title: Using silicon's extra bonds to hand off benzyl groups to azines
blurb: Aryl-equipped C1-silanes get activated by the same N-oxide handle sitting on the azine substrate, and fluoride-triggered [1,2]-shifts turn them into benzyl-like nucleophiles that land precisely at C2. Dense mechanistic chemistry, but the payoff is a genuinely new regiospecific way to homologate and arylate azines in one pot.

original_title: MOF‐Based Photothermal Catalysts for Solar Energy Conversion: Design Principles, Mechanistic Insights, and Applications in CO 2 Conversion and Hydrogen Production
title: Where MOF photothermal catalysis for solar fuels actually stands
blurb: A review rounding up design principles and mechanistic insight for MOF-based photothermal catalysts, the ones pairing light harvesting with heat-driven surface chemistry for CO2 conversion and hydrogen production. A map of the field rather than a new result.

original_title: A scFv-based immunotoxin for selective targeting and cytotoxicity against c-Met-overexpressing cancer cells: an integrated in silico and in vitro study
title: An amivantamab-derived antibody fragment with a venom payload bolted on
blurb: SM1 fuses an anti-c-Met scFv lifted from amivantamab to the cytolytic peptide melittin via flexible linkers, giving the fragment the killing power amivantamab itself lacks. In silico and in vitro only so far, but the logic is straightforward: receptor inhibition without cytolytic activity is half a drug.

original_title: Dosimetry and immunohistochemistry study to establish radiolabelled prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) as a potential theranostic target in high-grade glioma treatment.
title: Checking whether PSMA works as a target in brain tumors too
blurb: PSMA theranostics are mostly a prostate cancer story, so this dosimetry and immunohistochemistry work checks whether high-grade glioma expresses enough PSMA to make radiolabelled PSMA agents worth trying there as well. Thin on detail beyond that framing.

original_title: Truce–Smiles Rearrangement in Heterocyclic Synthesis: From Functional Groups to Framework
title: The Truce-Smiles rearrangement's heterocycle resume
blurb: A review tracking how the Truce-Smiles rearrangement, built on a spiro-Meisenheimer complex that spontaneously cascades apart, has been pressed into building heterocyclic scaffolds without any metal catalyst. Organized by intermediate size then by heterocycle type, so it reads more like a field atlas than a new reaction.

original_title: Nonheme Fe Enzyme-Catalyzed Enantioselective and Regiodivergent C(sp3)-H Amidation: Biocatalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of 1,2- and 1,3-Diamine Derivatives
title: An ethylene-biosynthesis enzyme repurposed to stamp out chiral diamines
blurb: Directed evolution turned ACC oxidase, a plant enzyme that normally just makes ethylene, into a biocatalyst family doing enantioselective, regiodivergent C(sp3)-H amidation, building cyclic ureas en route to 1,2- and 1,3-diamines straight from simple N-(benzoyloxy)urea substrates. It hits benzylic, allylic, propargylic, and plain unactivated C-H bonds with selectivity that chemocatalysis still struggles to match.

original_title: Dynamic 18 F-FDG Imaging of the Brain Using Total-Body PET in Patients with Genitourinary Cancer: A Pilot Study
title: Total-body PET watches FDG move through the brain in real time
blurb: A pilot using total-body PET's wide dynamic range to track dynamic FDG kinetics in the brains of genitourinary cancer patients. Pilot-scale, so it's a feasibility read on the imaging approach rather than any clinical finding.

original_title: Late-stage diversification of 5-hydroxyflavones by Suzuki–Miyaura and Buchwald–Hartwig cross-coupling
title: Running flavones through the usual Pd cross-coupling gauntlet
blurb: Suzuki-Miyaura and Buchwald-Hartwig coupling off a common halogenated 5-hydroxyflavone scaffold, itself scaled up to 10 g via an optimised Baker-Venkataraman route, gave sixteen biaryl flavones by conventional heating (41-93%) and thirteen diarylamino flavones under microwave (23-99%). Standard SAR-library chemistry, but the gram-scale precursor route is the part worth noting.

original_title: Towards an understanding of injury in aortic tissue prior to actual failure: quantification of mechanically induced collagen damage using collagen hybridizing peptides
title: Collagen hybridizing peptides catch aortic damage before the wall actually tears
blurb: Collagen hybridizing peptides bind selectively to mechanically unwound collagen, and the authors worked out a protocol to use them on large, loaded arteries instead of just small tissue samples, giving endovascular device testing a way to quantify damage before outright failure, which it previously couldn't do. Useful as a QA tool for device validation more than anything clinical.

original_title: Copolymerization of Ethylene and Allyl Acetate Using Nickel α-Diimine Complexes through Steric Control
title: Getting a nickel catalyst to swallow allyl acetate via steric control
blurb: Ni α-diimine complexes copolymerize ethylene with allyl acetate, a polar comonomer that normally poisons oxophilic nickel catalysts, by leaning on steric control at the ligand rather than electronic tuning. One of the few bidentate nickel systems reported that can even get this comonomer into the chain, aimed at functionalized polyethylene for blend compatibilizers.

original_title: Glycoform Distributions and Heparan Sulfate Binding of Intact SARS-CoV-2 Spike Variants by DIA-ECCR Native Mass Spectrometry
title: Mass spec sorts intact spike protein glycoforms variant by variant
blurb: A DIA-ECCR native mass spec workflow resolves glycoform distributions on intact SARS-CoV-2 spike across variants, including higher-mass subpopulations that bulk glycoproteomics usually blurs together, and ties the differences to heparan sulfate binding. Mostly a methods flex, but a genuinely useful one for tracking how glycosylation drifts as the spike evolves.

original_title: From Rim to Core: Nitrile Coordination Creates an Electronic Gradient across Cu12 Nanocluster Nodes for CO2-to-Formate Electrosynthesis
title: A nitrile ligand turns one face of a Cu12 cluster electron-poor on purpose
blurb: Nitrile coordination in a Cu12S9 MOF node creates a radially polarized cluster, with Bader analysis showing an electronic gradient running from the nitrile-bound rim to the thiolate-supported core, built for CO2-to-formate electrosynthesis. The interesting move is using the linker to differentiate equivalent metal sites rather than just stabilize the cluster, which is usually all reticulation gets asked to do.

original_title: ITM and AtomVie Global Radiopharma Enter Supply Agreement for n.c.a. Lutetium-177 - WBOC TV
title: ITM locks down another Lu-177 supplier
blurb: ITM signed a supply deal with AtomVie for non-carrier-added Lutetium-177, more capacity lining up behind the isotope every radioligand therapy pipeline is currently fighting over. A supply-chain story, not a data one.

original_title: Adaptive Active Site Programming via Electrolyte Engineering Toward Enhanced Catalytic Activity
title: Electrolyte anions quietly rewrite your single-atom catalyst's active site
blurb: Grand canonical DFT plus experiments on Fe-N-C single-atom ORR catalysts across five anions (F-, Cl-, Br-, NO3-, H2PO4-) show the electrolyte itself reshapes the active site's local coordination depending on pH and potential. Worth remembering next time a paper reports "the" active site structure as if it's fixed rather than whatever the electrolyte happened to leave behind.

original_title: Atomically Precise Platinum Nanocluster Catalysts for Efficient Hydrogen Production via Methylcyclohexane Dehydrogenation
title: Platinum clusters down to 17 atoms, still dehydrogenating methylcyclohexane
blurb: Atomically precise Pt17 and Pt~51 clusters on Al2O3 stay monodisperse (0.86 and 1.15 nm) and hold onto a cationic Ptδ+ state even through thermal treatment, with the smaller Pt17 posting the better mass activity for methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation, the step liquid organic hydrogen carriers need to release their H2. Smaller beating bigger isn't the usual story with supported metal catalysts.

original_title: Computational modeling and experimental validation of nitrile-thiol reactivity in Janus kinase inhibitors.
title: Mapping which nitriles in JAK inhibitors actually react with thiols
blurb: Covalent JAK inhibitors depend on a nitrile warhead grabbing a cysteine thiol, and this pairs computation with experiment to sort out which nitrile environments actually fire and which just sit there looking reactive. The useful output is a design rule, not just a confirmation that the chemistry works.

original_title: Partnership will expand access to Lutetium-177 for radiopharmaceutical developers - Radiology Business
title: Another company lines up to get you Lutetium-177
blurb: A partnership meant to widen access to Lu-177 for radiopharmaceutical developers. Mostly a supply-chain story: everyone's designing trials around an isotope that's still the bottleneck to actually get enough of.

original_title: Multiscale Modeling of Virus Capsid Self-Assembly Reveals How Small Molecule Antivirals Can Redirect Assembly Pathways and Products
title: Modeling shows how HBV capsid drugs sabotage the build rather than just stop it
blurb: A kinetic Monte Carlo model of hepatitis B capsid assembly tracks how CAM small molecules reroute the process into malformed, nonfunctional shells instead of simply halting it. The mechanism's been murky, and this is a simulation answer rather than a structural one, so treat it as a well-argued hypothesis, not a solved structure.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Functional -PO2-mediated asymmetric CuN3 site enabled synergistic acetylene hydrochlorination
title: Breaking the symmetry of a CuN4 site to make acetylene hydrochlorination work harder
blurb: Symmetric copper-N4 single-atom sites are the usual setup and they underperform because the substrate never gets polarized enough. P-doping here knocks one nitrogen out, leaving an asymmetric CuN3 site next to a dangling -PO2 group, and the pair act like an enzyme pocket for acetylene hydrochlorination. Neat microenvironment trick, though single-atom catalysts have a habit of not surviving scale-up.

original_title: 8-Oxoguanine Is the Major Product of the Reaction of Guanine Radical Cations with •NO2: A Spin-Orchestrated, Anisotropic Reaction Landscape and Its Biological Implications
title: How NO2 radicals push guanine damage toward 8-oxoguanine
blurb: Guanine radical cations are already a textbook DNA lesion from radiation and one-electron oxidation, and this maps what happens when they meet the reactive nitrogen species NO2: 8-oxoguanine comes out as the dominant product, via a spin-dependent, direction-sensitive reaction path. Mechanistic chemistry with an obvious mutagenesis angle riding along.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: The effect of inorganic impurities in post-consumer plastic waste on the catalytic cracking of polyolefins
title: The crud already in your plastic waste is messing with catalytic cracking
blurb: Post-consumer polyolefin waste doesn't just carry polymer, it carries inorganic impurities too, and this looks at what those do to catalytic cracking performance. Light on specifics here, but it's the real-world contamination problem that lab-grade feedstock studies usually skip past.

original_title: ReConLiG: Reaction-Guided Design of Organometallic Ligands via Decoupled Generative Pretraining and Contrastive Alignment
title: A ligand-generating model that skips the labeled-reaction dataset
blurb: ReConLiG first learns a ligand latent space from 500,000 unlabeled Sadphos pseudo-ligands, then uses contrastive alignment to steer generation toward a given reaction, instead of fine-tuning on labeled reaction data every time. Decoupling those two steps is the actual trick, since labeled organometallic data is the thing nobody has enough of.

original_title: Beyond active sites: reaction field engineering for heterogeneous CO 2 hydrogenation toward formic acid and formate
title: Formic acid from CO2 is a reactor-design problem as much as a catalyst problem
blurb: A framework for tuning the whole reaction field together, active sites, local environment, spatial layout, reactor operation, rather than chasing a better catalyst in isolation for CO2 hydrogenation to formic acid and formate. Reads more like a thesis statement than a result, but the reframing is the point.

original_title: Broad-Spectrum Synthesis of Spiro[oxazolidine-2-thione-oxindoles] and Oxazolidine-2-thiones via CS2-Mediated Reactions of Isatins and α-Keto Carbonyl Compounds
title: One pot, CS2, and a pile of new spiro-oxindole scaffolds
blurb: A CS2-mediated multicomponent reaction stitches amino acid esters together with isatins or acyclic keto esters/amides to build spiro[oxazolidine-2-thione-oxindoles] and plain oxazolidine-2-thiones, setting a new stereocenter and tolerating a broad range of functional groups, under mild conditions and in high yield. A scaffold-generation paper, but a genuinely broad one.

original_title: Diastereoselective synthesis of 3-monosubstituted phthalides through the MCR of phthalaldehydic acid, sulfoxonium ylides and thiols
title: Phthalaldehydic acid, sulfoxonium ylides, and thiols combine into clean phthalides
blurb: A Bronsted acid-catalyzed three-component reaction builds 3-monosubstituted phthalides with a thiol hanging off the side chain, in moderate to good yield and excellent anti-diastereoselectivity across different thiols, ylides, and phthalaldehydic acids. Mild conditions and solid selectivity for a motif that keeps turning up in natural product synthesis.

original_title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis
title: Enzymes that make poison without poisoning themselves
blurb: Natural product biosynthesis often runs through redox chemistry reactive enough to kill the cell that makes it. This looks at how a biosynthetic pathway balances that cytotoxic risk against the catalysis it actually needs to build the molecule.

original_title: High-Throughput Coded Aperture Raman Imaging with Total Internal Reflection
title: Getting Raman imaging past its throughput problem without splitting the laser
blurb: Spontaneous Raman is label-free but scatters so weakly that large-area hyperspectral imaging is painfully slow. TIRR bounces the excitation inside a thin sapphire slab for extended evanescent illumination instead of dividing the beam across separate spots, then pairs it with Hadamard-coded detection to pull spatially resolved spectra back out. A way to buy throughput without giving up laser power per point.

original_title: Synthesis, Structure, and Magnetic Properties of a Series of Trinuclear Heterometallic 3 d –4 f Complexes
title: A 3d-4f sandwich complex that comes out opposite-handed at each end
blurb: A series of linear Ln-TM-Ln complexes (La, Pr, Nd flanking a Co or Mn center) made by reducing the neutral precursor with cobaltocene, which leaves cobalticinium as the counterion. The crystals land in a noncentrosymmetric space group, and the two outer lanthanide centers settle into opposite chirality despite sitting in the same molecule. Structural trivia until the magnetic data land, but a neat trick of crystallization.

original_title: HFn-E2: a computationally designed human H-ferritin nanocage codelivering iron and the covalent GPX4 inhibitor ML210 for ferroptosis induction in lung cancer — design, PBPK scenario modelling, structure validation and human-data premise analysis
title: A ferritin cage designed to haul iron and a GPX4 killer together
blurb: HFn-E2 is a computationally designed human ferritin nanocage meant to pack both a mineralized iron core and ML210, the potent covalent GPX4 inhibitor nobody's put in a protein cage before, aiming to dump both into TfR1-positive lung tumors and tip them into ferroptosis once the cage breaks down in the lysosome. What's here is the design, the PBPK modeling, and structure validation, not an efficacy readout, so it's a blueprint rather than a result so far.

original_title: Monoclonal antibodies for detecting collagen IV α3α4α5 in basement membranes
title: First antibodies that see the assembled collagen IV 345 trimer, not just its parts
blurb: Alport syndrome comes from mutations that keep the collagen IV alpha3alpha4alpha5 trimer from assembling properly in basement membranes, but the antibody tools around until now only picked up individual chains. They built a recombinant mini-trimer to raise mouse monoclonals against the native assembled complex itself, screening hits by biolayer interferometry, native dot blot, and denaturing western. A diagnostic tool more than a therapy, but one that's been missing.

original_title: Bilayer coated lipid nanoparticles as a platform for orthogonal design of core and surface properties
title: Giving LNPs a separate dial for the core and the surface
blurb: Standard lipid nanoparticles are one compartment doing everything, so encapsulation efficiency, endosomal escape, stability, and targeting all fight over the same formulation knobs. Coating the core in a second lipid bilayer lets the two layers be engineered independently, which in principle opens up formulation space a single-compartment LNP just doesn't have.

original_title: Gypsophila Pattern of HCC Recurrence Detected by 68 Ga-Labeled Antiglypican-3 Single-Chain Variable Fragment PET/MRI After Liver Transplantation
title: A GPC3-targeted PET tracer picks up a distinctive scatter pattern of HCC relapse after transplant
blurb: Ga-68 labeled anti-glypican-3 antibody fragment PET/MRI picks up hepatocellular carcinoma recurring after liver transplant in a diffuse, scattered pattern, which the authors name the 'Gypsophila pattern' after the flower's spray of small blooms.

original_title: Cysteine-Conjugated Antibody-Drug Conjugate (ADC) Production and Characterization.
title: A step-by-step for cysteine-linked ADCs
blurb: A Methods in Molecular Biology protocol for producing and characterizing cysteine-conjugated ADCs, the standard thiol-maleimide route rather than anything new. A lab manual chapter, not a finding.

original_title: Synthesis of Site-Specific Antibody-Drug Conjugates via Endoglycosidase-Catalyzed Fc Glycan Remodeling.
title: Glycan remodeling as the site-specific ADC route
blurb: A protocol using endoglycosidases to trim and remodel the Fc glycan, then hang the payload off that one defined site instead of random cysteines or lysines. Site-specific conjugation via glycoengineering rather than mutagenesis.

original_title: Development and In Vitro Evaluation of [(225)Ac]Ac-DOTATATE for Targeted Alpha Therapy of Neuroblastoma.
title: An Ac-225-DOTATATE conjugate aimed at neuroblastoma, tested in vitro
blurb: DOTATATE targets somatostatin receptors, labeled here with Actinium-225 for alpha therapy and put through in vitro evaluation against neuroblastoma. Development-stage cell work, nothing dosed in an animal yet.
